ops.title: daemon test rig: trust verifier self-probe flakes under constrained CPU (1.5s spawn window)
ops.description:
The daemon package's Begin-time trust verifier self-probe inherits the rig's 3s budget minus the worker's 1.5s totalReserve, leaving ~1.5s to fork/exec a race-instrumented child. Under load (local, load avg 14-38) or on constrained CI runners this intermittently fails: `daemon: trust verifier self-probe failed ... worker: timed out / context deadline exceeded`.

Evidence: bisected 2026-07-25 across three trees under matched load (pristine HEAD / feature-only / fixed) with failures 5/3/4 per 3 rounds — present at pristine baseline, load-driven, not caused by the settlement change. First observed on CI itself 2026-07-25 (run 30178033882, TestProductSettlementClaimIsSingularStartingAndGenerationFenced, ubuntu-latest, 1.54s); the 15 prior CI runs were green, consistent with an intermittent load-sensitive flake rather than a deterministic regression.

Fix shape: raise the daemon test rig's Begin budget (runtimeTestTimeout 3s → enough that the probe keeps >3s headroom), or decouple the probe budget from the rig budget. Touches ~32 rig call sites — mechanical but wide, which is why it was ruled out of the settlement task's scope.

Sequencing: post-baseline (release freeze until fleet convergence); this flake will otherwise tax every future daemonkit push with rerun roulette.

ops.text: scripts/test.sh -race ./daemon/... passes 10 consecutive runs on a 2-core runner (or under load avg > 15 locally)
the trust verifier self-probe budget no longer derives from the rig's 3s test timeout
